response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT link_to_member, SUM(amount) AS s FROM income GROUP BY link_to_member), sh AS (SELECT s, s * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(s) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS av FROM sh) SELECT SUM(sh.s) AS total_amount, AVG(sh.share) AS avg_share, AVG(sh.share - a.av) AS avg_share_minus_avg FROM sh CROSS JOIN a WHERE sh.share > a.av

assumptions.assumption: A missing link_to_member means NULL only. GROUP BY puts all NULLs into one group, and that group counts like any other. Empty strings are not treated as missing and form their own group, if there are any.
Shares are computed with floating-point division, with no rounding. Groups whose summed amount is NULL (all amounts NULL) still count as groups, with a NULL sum.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat both NULL and empty-string link_to_member as missing and put them together in one group.
alternatives.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT NULLIF(TRIM(link_to_member), '') AS m, SUM(amount) AS s FROM income GROUP BY NULLIF(TRIM(link_to_member), '')), sh AS (SELECT s, s * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(s) FROM g) AS share FROM g), a AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS av FROM sh) SELECT SUM(sh.s) AS total_amount, AVG(sh.share) AS avg_share, AVG(sh.share - a.av) AS avg_share_minus_avg FROM sh CROSS JOIN a WHERE sh.share > a.av
